description:
An unknown threat actor has infected 953 online stores, most of them running Magento, as part of a long-running campaign active since July 2025.

According to Dutch e-commerce security company Sansec, the activity is designed to add a small piece of code to the store's pages that, when visited by unsuspecting users, serves malicious JavaScript loader code through Magento CMS blocks.

title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento

description:
PHP has rebuilt its official Windows packages for PHP 8.2 through 8.5 to fix CVE-2026-111497, a flaw in the Brotli compression library that the packages include. The flaw can let an attacker corrupt memory and potentially run code.

PHP says the flaw can be reached through the cURL extension when the extension decompresses HTTP responses automatically. cURL leaves that off by default, but
title: PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw

description:
This2Shell, That2Shell, Everything2Shell. That's pretty much how the last week went. Critical bugs that let attackers run code remotely are showing up everywhere. title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: This2Shell, That2Shell, Everything's an RCE? Rogue AI, Supply Chain Chaos and More

description:
Two critical flaws in Wasmtime, a WebAssembly runtime that can be built into other software, could allow a malicious WebAssembly module to escape the sandbox intended to contain it, the project's maintainers say.

An attacker would first need a vulnerable Wasmtime build to compile a module they control, and one of the flaws affects only ARM64 systems. Fixed versions were released on
title: Two Critical Wasmtime Flaws Could Let Malicious WebAssembly Modules Escape Sandboxes

description:
Every SOC struggles with a pile of alerts. Very few of those alerts explain how an attack started or how it progressed. Network data, like that from a network detection and response (NDR) platform, connects individual alerts into one timeline, and it feeds the defensive systems that can tie all events together into one coordinated view.

title: Between alerts: What Attackers Do in the Spaces Ordinary Detection Misses

description:
A rentable Android spyware kit called uCreator takes over Telegram and WeChat accounts by hiding its code inside working copies of the two apps, researcher Ovi found. It only reaches people who install one of these tampered copies, spread outside the official app stores, or who run WeChat inside the kit makers' own container app.

title: uCreator Android Spyware Can Steal Telegram 2FA Passwords and Clone WeChat Accounts

description:
An automated campaign is using stolen GitHub tokens to plant workflows that print a repository's secrets into its GitHub Actions logs, which the attackers then download before deleting the runs. title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs

description:
A malicious instruction file sitting in a developer's Downloads folder tried to make their AI coding agent install a known-malicious npm package, security firm Forever Security said in a report published last week.

The company caught the attempt on a real customer's machine and stopped the agent before any code ran. It could not determine how the file got into the folder.
